lines:
Fixed the 32k bug by replacing the absolute floor with a derived one; commit 3173c99 on main. The agreed budget model is "aim every compaction at a quarter of the window", so the numbers here supersede the R/U/S model on task 142 (see that task's memo).

PART 1 (floor over-refuses): MINIMUM_COMPACT_CONTEXT_WINDOW is deleted, with automatic_compaction_available, working_headroom, user_budget and summary_budget. Policy now exposes target(window) = floor(0.25 W), replacement_plan(window, fixed) -> ReplacementPlan { retain, summary }, can_reduce(window, fixed), minimum_window(fixed) and compaction_advisory(window, fixed). The floor is derived: minimum_window(fixed) = ceil((fixed + 2,512) / 0.25), which for the recorded Chat (fixed about 12,300) is 59,248 - the same territory as the 64,000 constant, but it now moves with the measured tool selection instead of being chosen. Both tests that pinned "64000" were rewritten; the policy test now asserts minimum_window(12_400) == 59_648 and that the advisory names 5,9648/2,512/25% and says compaction runs anyway.

PART 2 (declared window never enforced, 47 warnings): automatic compaction now runs for any declared window unless the fixed context already reaches the trigger (can_reduce) or the fixed context cannot be measured (fixed_tokens error). Below the floor the plan clamps to exactly the minima (retain 2,000, summary 512) instead of the 2,959 the first draft produced, so can_reduce, minimum_window and the advisory all promise the same 2,512 tokens and one clamped compaction provably lands below the 0.8 trigger. Warnings go through the new RunEventStream::context_advisory_once, which publishes one event per distinct body, clears the condition when the advisory disappears, and re-arms on recurrence. The unknown-window advisory uses the same path. So the 32k run now compacts every ~4.9 turns at fixed 12,300 and never exceeds 0.8 W; the 47-warning pathology is structurally impossible.

PART 3 (fs arithmetic): fixed_tokens now documents what it measures and what it excludes, with the measured numbers that make a 32k window marginal: turn 3 of the recorded run reported 12,426 input tokens, about 12,300 of them fixed (workspace and per-tool instructions plus 31 tool schemas). That is why the derived floor lands near 59,000 and why the honest advice for a small window is a smaller tool selection as much as a smaller replacement budget.

BUDGET ARITHMETIC NOW IN FORCE (fixed 12,400): 32k -> retain 2,000 / summary 512 (clamped, target missed, one advisory); 100k -> 7,787 / 4,813; 262k -> 45,136 / 8,000; 1M -> 241,744 / 8,000. The last three land exactly on 0.25 W, and the retained tail grows with the window while the summary stops at its 8,000 cap - a large-context model keeps proportionally more history verbatim instead of paying for a bigger summary. The carried-user budget U is gone; user turns ride inside the tail at up to half of it. The provider output reservation is clamped to the same quarter share, so 393,216 output tokens declared against a 32,000-token window no longer collapse the window to zero.

VERIFICATION: full desktop lib suite 484 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the pre-existing ignore); capability-host suite 176 + 18 passed. Rewritten tests: budgets_are_derived_from_the_target_window (targets at 32k/100k/262k/1M, exact-target landing, clamped plan, minimum_window, can_reduce boundary at 18,640/18,642, advisory text, manual zero retention); a_window_whose_target_is_out_of_reach_still_compacts_and_reports_once (a 32k window whose fixed context sits between target and trigger compacts with the clamped plan, pays for exactly one summary, ends under the trigger, records exactly one advisory naming the derived window, and stays quiet on the next turn); the two integration tests that pinned a 1,280-token summary cap now derive it from the policy for their own window and fixed context.

NOT DONE, deliberately: Part 4 (a segmented or map-reduce summary for a prefix that no longer fits the window, or a lossy drop when the summary keeps failing) is untouched. With the always-run compaction the 32k run now compacts rather than growing, so the fitting lossy reduction Part 2 asked for is not needed for the acceptance case; ContextOverflow (retain 0 plus pruning, one attempt) remains the lossy path when the provider reports overflow. Recorded as its own task.

ALSO FIXED, unrelated and pre-existing: crates/aworkit-capability-host/tests/provider_protocols.rs had been red since a177787 - it still expected ModelCacheUsageV1::default() while the OpenAI-compatible adapter now reports sent_bytes/common_prefix_bytes. Commit f5fec20 asserts the adapter's actual promise (two chunks, usage with non-zero sent_bytes and a zero first-request prefix) instead of the serialized body size.

ONE KNOWN FLAKE, unrelated to the policy: with the whole lib suite in parallel, an_exhausted_summary_recovery_warns_once_and_keeps_the_selection failed once at its first assertion (provider_error was None) and passes alone and on every full-suite rerun since, including three consecutive runs of its own module. Every compaction test registers the same binding id "model.compaction-test"/"v1" in the shared gateway registry, so a parallel sibling can serve a request; worth a per-test binding id, but it is a harness issue rather than a policy defect.

FOLLOW-UP RECORDED: retainRatio/retainTokens in CompactionSettings.tsx ("Retained history budget") no longer control a windowed Chat's tail, which is now derived from the target; the field only affects the legacy path for a Chat with no declared window (and there the ratio was already inert because it is multiplied by a zero window). The setting needs a UI decision rather than a silent change.

A declared 32,000-token window was not respected: automatic compaction is disabled below a hard 64,000-token floor, so the run never compacted, warned once per turn, and grew to 142,887 prompt tokens (4.5x the declared window) until the operator cancelled it.

Run: run.dc494327fb61fde93f9322e599724dce6a45430f / chat.dc494327fb61fde93f9322e599724dce6a45430f, project test1_*, same Tetris prompt, model deepseek-flash with contextWindow 32000 frozen in chat.frozen-sessions (no summarization target, default policy). Evidence: 46 model turns, peak prompt 142,887 tokens, 47 context.compaction-warning events (one per turn) and ZERO context.compaction-started/compacted events; the three span.failed entries at seq 7408-7410 are the operator's cancellation ("provider execution was cancelled"). The warning text is the app's own: "Automatic compaction needs a declared context window of at least 64000 tokens; this model declares 32000."

Part 1 - the floor over-refuses (real bug, small fix). desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/compaction/mod.rs:339 MINIMUM_COMPACT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 64_000 short-circuits automatic_compaction_available before the derived check at line 327, which is the actual rule ("one checkpoint must leave a quarter of the window"). Its own unit test proves the over-refusal: automatic_compaction_available(32_768, 3_000) would pass the derived check (headroom 12,729; x4 = 50,917 >= 32,768) yet is refused by the constant and asserted to say "64000". Fix: delete the constant and let the headroom check decide, so the message names the real constraint. Update the two tests that pin 64000 (compaction/tests.rs:389, compaction/integration_tests.rs:276).

Part 2 - the declared window is never enforced (the defect that actually hurt). When automatic summarisation is unavailable the app only warns and keeps going: 47 warnings and no reduction, because the provider's real window is 1M so no overflow error ever arrived to trigger the ContextOverflow path. With a provider that enforced 32k the same run would have died. Fix: when pressure reaches the declared window (or the threshold with no available compaction), reduce with a strategy that always fits - drop the oldest exchanges/tool results, keep user turns and a recent tail, reusing the selection machinery in compaction/runtime.rs (retain=0 for ContextOverflow). Emit the diagnostic once per condition, not once per turn.

Part 3 - why removing the floor alone would not have fixed this run (measured arithmetic). fixed_tokens (system messages + tool schemas + notice, surface.rs:178) is about 12,300 for this Chat: turn 3 reports input 12,426 with estimated 12,596, and the stable header measured 12,032 on test1_3. With threshold 0.8 x 32,000 = 25,600 and the default replacement budget (retention 16% + user 8% + summary 8% = 32% of the window = 10,240), headroom = 25,600 - 10,240 - 12,300 = 3,060, and the quarter-window rule needs 8,000. So at 32k the derived check refuses too, truthfully: the fixed context plus the default budgets cannot leave room to work. Two ways to make 32k actually compact: scale the replacement budget for small windows (a 12k fixed context needs replacement <= about 17% of the window), or shrink the fixed context itself - 37 advertised tool schemas plus a 13 KB system prompt is what makes 32k marginal, which is exactly what the second warning advises ("Use a larger-context model or a smaller tool selection").

Part 4 - follow-up, larger: the summary call sends the entire prefix in one request (measured 156,336 input tokens / 540 KB on the qwen run), so it can only ever work while the prefix fits the window. A context already at 142k on a 32k window cannot be summarised in one call; small windows need a segmented or map-reduce summary, or a lossy drop instead.

Acceptance: a 32k-window run either compacts (once Part 1/Part 3 budgets allow) or degrades with a fitting lossy reduction, never exceeding its declared window; the diagnostic is emitted once and names the real constraint; no regression in the large-window runs (test1_3 stays at 64,192 uncached and 9/9 conformance).

data.title: A declared 32k window is never enforced: the 64k compaction floor blocks it and nothing else acts
